title: No other gospel (Galatians 1)
hookLine: Paul, alarmed, tells his story: not from people but from revelation
tomorrow: Peter moves his plate to another table. why does Paul go off?
last: THE GOD WHO RAISES · A SWEET SAVOR · A LIVING LETTER

cards: "You only believe that because your parents do." Some version of that line turns up in comment sections, at lunch tables, at a holiday dinner. Paul heard his own version.
In Galatia, some seem to have said his message was secondhand. And he's alarmed: "I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel."
This isn't about other religions. It's a quarrel inside the young churches over what the good news is.

teach.b: Paul's answer isn't an argument. It's his story.
"I certify you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached of me is not after man. For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ."
He doesn't polish his past: "beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it." Then the turn, and it isn't his own doing.
God "called me by his grace, To reveal his Son in me." Then a small detail with a lot of warmth.
Churches in Judea that had never seen his face heard only this: "he which persecuted us in times past now preacheth the faith which once he destroyed. And they glorified God in me."
The people he once harmed praised God because of him.
Writing to Corinth, he put the whole thing in one line: "But by the grace of God I am what I am."

how: In some churches people share a testimony, the story of how they came to faith; others mark the same story through baptism, confirmation or a quiet word with a friend.

games.q: your friend's little brother asks her, 'did you pick your faith, or did mom pick it for you?' what fits Paul's way of answering?
o: tell her own story honestly: what she received, and what became hers.
call the question rude, and refuse to answer it at all.
say real faith has to start with a dramatic vision, like Paul's.
games.why: Paul answers 'secondhand?' with his story, told plainly: who he was, what turned, and by the grace of God I am what I am.

practice: Say your own story out loud in three short sentences: where you started, what turned, where you are now. It can be about faith, or about whatever you hold most dear, and it needs no drama.
Then, if it fits, say Paul's line after it: by the grace of God I am what I am.

wordCard.voice: No other gospel. Paul's alarm when the good news was being changed, and his answer: his own story.

orig.note: Greek: good news, gospel; the word at the center of Galatians 1.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: by the grace of God, the whole of Paul's story in a single line. Week done.
